Alternatively, the braid γn can be described as follows: arrange the points labeled
by the numbers 1 up to ns in a rectangular pattern with height n and width s. Now
we can numerate the points either by ﬁrst going down the columns, or by ﬁrst going
to the right in each row. This deﬁnes a permutation π mapping the i-th point in
the column-ﬁrst count to the i-th point in the row-ﬁrst count. The braid γn is now
deﬁned by this permutation where the i-th lower point is connected with the π(i)-
th upper point and where we assume all crossings to be positive (i.e., the strand
going from southwest to northeast crosses over the one going from southeast to
northwest). A picture for this braid can be found in [Erlijman 2003, p. 83].
